# rules/

The LLM's operating manual: 25 numbered rule files distilling Marshall Allen's methodology and US consumer-protection law into the tactics the model follows at each stage of the dispute process, from first principles through insurance appeal, small claims, and specialty billing situations.

<!-- BEGIN CONTENTS (auto-generated, do not edit by hand) -->

- [00_principles.md](00_principles.md): These three facts about US medical billing precede every tactic in this kit.
- [01_never_pay_first.md](01_never_pay_first.md): A medical bill is not a demand for immediate payment.
- [02_request_itemization.md](02_request_itemization.md): You cannot dispute a bill you can't see.
- [03_check_cpt_codes.md](03_check_cpt_codes.md): Each line on an itemized bill carries a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) or HCPCS code.
- [04_no_surprises_act.md](04_no_surprises_act.md): The federal No Surprises Act (effective January 1, 2022) makes certain categories of "surprise" medical bills illegal.
- [05_negotiate_fair_price.md](05_negotiate_fair_price.md): When a bill is correctly coded for a service you actually received but the price is unreasonable, the dispute is about price, not error.
- [06_small_claims.md](06_small_claims.md): Small claims court is the single biggest piece of leverage a patient has against a provider or insurer.
- [07_appeal_insurance_denial.md](07_appeal_insurance_denial.md): When the insurance company denies coverage, the dispute is between you and the insurer, not you and the provider.
- [08_avoid_unneeded_care.md](08_avoid_unneeded_care.md): The bill you don't receive is the one you don't have to dispute.
- [09_pricing_resources.md](09_pricing_resources.md): Most care is not emergency care.
- [10_ground_ambulance.md](10_ground_ambulance.md): The federal No Surprises Act explicitly excludes ground ambulance from its balance-billing protections.
- [11_ppdr_walkthrough.md](11_ppdr_walkthrough.md): For uninsured and self-pay patients whose final bill exceeds the Good Faith Estimate (GFE) they were entitled to receive.
- [12_medicare_appeals.md](12_medicare_appeals.md): Medicare uses a five-level appeal structure that is entirely different from ERISA-plan or commercial-plan appeals.
- [13_emtala.md](13_emtala.md): EMTALA is the federal statute that prevents hospitals participating in Medicare from "dumping" patients with emergency conditions or active labor.
- [14_hipaa_right_of_access.md](14_hipaa_right_of_access.md): A patient's right to obtain a copy of their own medical records is a federal entitlement, not a courtesy the provider may grant or deny at will.
- [15_auto_med_pay.md](15_auto_med_pay.md): When a patient is treated for injuries from a motor-vehicle accident, the billing path is different from ordinary medical billing.
- [16_workers_comp.md](16_workers_comp.md): When an injury or illness arises out of and in the course of employment, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy in nearly all US states.
- [17_bankruptcy_and_medical_debt.md](17_bankruptcy_and_medical_debt.md): Medical debt is the leading cause of US personal bankruptcy.
- [18_tricare.md](18_tricare.md): TRICARE is the health-care program for active-duty service members, retirees, National Guard and Reserve members, and their families.
- [19_va_community_care.md](19_va_community_care.md): Veterans who receive care from non-VA providers under the VA Community Care program are protected from direct billing by federal law.
- [20_telehealth.md](20_telehealth.md): Telehealth went from niche to mainstream during COVID-19 and has remained mainstream.
- [21_section_1557.md](21_section_1557.md): Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act prohibits discrimination in healthcare on the bases of race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability, at any healthcare program or activity receiving…
- [22_air_ambulance.md](22_air_ambulance.md): Air ambulance (helicopter EMS, fixed-wing critical-care transport) is covered by the federal No Surprises Act, unlike ground ambulance, which is the federal NSA's biggest gap.
- [23_aca_marketplace.md](23_aca_marketplace.md): ACA marketplace plans (purchased on healthcare.gov or a state-based exchange) are subject to a distinct federal appeals framework that differs from both ERISA self-funded plans and Medicare.
- [24_observation_status.md](24_observation_status.md): A Medicare patient admitted to a hospital may be placed in either "inpatient" status or "observation" (outpatient) status.
